correctness.rationale: Actual RESULT.md uses the unique contractive periodic disease-free state of dot S=mu(1-S) with instantaneous strengths p,q,r in (0,1). For two pulses, deficit J satisfies J_A=p+(1-p)E J_B/x and J_B=q+(1-q)xJ_A, giving mean bar S=1-[(p+q)(1-E)+2Epq-pq(x+E/x)]/(mu T D). The positive curvature x+E/x is uniquely minimized at x=sqrt E, hence tau=T/2 for all unequal strengths. Peak equals 1-min{A(x),B(x)}, with A increasing and B decreasing and exactly one intersection x*=[E(p-q)+sqrt(E²(p-q)²+4pqE)]/(2p). Half spacing coincides with minimax iff p=q. For three pulses, cyclic J recurrences and constraint xyz=E yield constrained gradient components p(q-r)(u-1)/D3 and r(q-p)(u-1)/D3 at x=y=z=u, which vanish jointly iff p=q=r; hence unequal strengths make equal spacing nonstationary, NOT a global three-pulse minimizer classification. Independently recalculated both symbolic gradients with SymPy and exact witness F_equal=257/253 versus F_unequal=2573/2530 (positive difference 3/2530). The scalar infected Floquet multiplier exp[T(beta bar S-delta)] is monotone in mean S only under constant beta,delta.

value.rationale: Scheduling pulses to reduce cumulative invasion potential versus worst instantaneous susceptibility is a natural epidemiological optimization tradeoff. The theorem establishes a sharp two-to-three intervention change: two heterogeneous campaigns optimally split mean-risk time equally, while three heterogeneous campaigns cannot be stationary at equal gaps. These exact phase and constraint boundaries can guide model comparison even without nonlinear epidemic predictions.
